events.title: New Liberty Standard publishes an early BTC exchange rate

research.summary: New Liberty Standard published an exchange rate of $1 = 1,309.03 BTC based on estimated electricity cost.
research.significance: An early attempt to express Bitcoin in dollar terms before liquid exchange markets existed.

research.summary: Hal Finney posted the two-word status 'Running bitcoin' while operating the early software.
research.significance: It is one of the earliest public signs of a second known Bitcoin participant and an iconic cultural artifact.

research.summary: Bitcoin v0.1, including source code, was made publicly available on SourceForge after Satoshi's 8 January UTC announcement.
research.significance: This turned Bitcoin from a paper into runnable open-source software.

sources.title: Bitcoin v0.1 released — Cryptography Mailing List

events.title: Satoshi embeds the Times headline in the Genesis Block

research.summary: The Genesis Block embeds the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.'
research.significance: The message serves as a timestamp anchor and became a lasting symbol of Bitcoin's historical context.

events.title: Hal Finney receives the first Bitcoin transaction from Satoshi

research.summary: This row is the same first 10 BTC Satoshi-to-Finney transfer.

events.title: Martti Malmi makes an early known Bitcoin-for-fiat sale

research.summary: New Liberty Standard bought 5,050 BTC from Martti Malmi for $5.02 via PayPal, an early documented BTC-for-fiat trade.
research.significance: A key step from theoretical valuation toward real monetary exchange.

events.title: Satoshi and Hal Finney discuss early Bitcoin bugs and performance

research.summary: Surviving emails show Satoshi and Hal Finney debugging early Bitcoin networking/software issues during launch week.
research.significance: Provides unusually direct evidence of the practical engineering work behind Bitcoin's first days.

events.title: Bitcoin client source code is released publicly

research.summary: This row describes the public release of Bitcoin's client/source code.

sources.title: Bitcoin v0.1 released — Cryptography Mailing List

events.title: Early miners collect 50 BTC block rewards on CPUs

research.summary: Bitcoin v0.1 was configured for CPU generation with an intentionally easy initial difficulty and 50 BTC block subsidy.
research.significance: Captures the hobbyist CPU-mining era before GPU and ASIC specialization.

sources.title: Bitcoin v0.1 released — Cryptography Mailing List

research.summary: Bitcoin's genesis block was timestamped 3 January 2009 and contains the Times bank-bailout headline in its coinbase data.
research.significance: The genesis block created the chain's starting point and one of crypto's most iconic historical artifacts.

research.summary: Block 170 contains the first known person-to-person Bitcoin transfer: 10 BTC sent by Satoshi to Hal Finney.
research.significance: The first known Bitcoin transaction between two people proved the network could transfer value.

events.title: Satoshi opens the new Bitcoin forum

research.summary: Satoshi posted 'Welcome to the new Bitcoin forum!' on 22 November 2009, pointing users to the older SourceForge forum and beginning the forum archive later known as BitcoinTalk.
research.significance: The forum became the central surviving public record of much of Bitcoin's formative technical discussion, commerce, culture and Satoshi-era community activity.

sources.title: Satoshi Nakamoto Institute — Welcome to the new Bitcoin forum

events.title: Bitcoin difficulty increases for the first time

research.summary: At block 32,256, Bitcoin's mining difficulty increased from 1.00 to about 1.18 for the first time.
research.significance: The first upward retarget was direct on-chain evidence that mining participation had grown enough for Bitcoin's automatic difficulty mechanism to raise the work requirement.

sources.title: Satoshi Nakamoto Institute — Proof-of-work difficulty increasing
